name: Four New Years (Arba Roshei Shanim)
notes: The four different new year dates for different purposes: kings, festivals, animal tithes, trees, vegetables, shemitah/yovel

name: New Year for Kings (Rosh HaShanah laMelachim)
notes: First of Nisan as the new year for counting years of a king's reign

name: New Year for Trees (Rosh HaShanah laIlanot)
notes: Tu b'Shevat (Beit Hillel) or 1 Shevat (Beit Shammai) as the cutoff for fruit tithes; distinct from the general Tu b'Shevat entry in that it addresses the halakhic mechanism of tithing

name: New Year for Animal Tithes
notes: First of Elul (or 1 Tishrei per R. Elazar and R. Shimon) as the cutoff date for grouping animals for maaser beheimah

name: Divine Judgment on Rosh HaShanah
notes: The concept that all creatures pass before God like sheep (bnei maron) on Rosh HaShanah; also judgment on Pesach for grain, Shavuot for fruit, Sukkot for water

name: Witnesses for Sanctifying the New Month
notes: Rules for qualification, examination, and acceptance of witnesses who testify about sighting the new moon; desecrating Shabbat to bring testimony; disqualification of relatives and others

name: Messengers Sent Out for New Month (Shelichei Beit Din)
notes: The six months in which messengers were dispatched to inform the Diaspora of the new moon; later replaced by torch signals; historical and legal background

name: Torch Signals for the New Moon (Massuot)
notes: The original system of lighting torches on mountaintops to relay the news of the new month; discontinued due to Samaritan interference

name: Beit Ya'azek (Witness Assembly Court)
notes: The Jerusalem courtyard where witnesses for the new moon gathered; Rabban Gamliel's institution of 2000-cubit movement rights for witnesses and others who arrived on Shabbat

name: Examination of New Moon Witnesses
notes: The procedure for examining witnesses about the shape, position, and direction of the new moon; Rabban Gamliel's diagram of lunar forms

name: Declaration of the New Month (Mekudash)
notes: The formal pronouncement by the head of the court 'It is sanctified' and communal response; whether sanctification is needed when moon was not seen at anticipated time

name: Types and Materials of the Shofar
notes: Which animals' horns are valid for shofar; cow horn disqualified; ibex (straight) for Rosh HaShanah Temple service; ram's horn for fast days; cracked or repaired shofarot

name: Shofar in the Temple vs. Provinces
notes: Distinctions between shofar practice in the Temple (with gold-mouthed ibex horn + two silver trumpets) and elsewhere; shofar on Shabbat only in Temple or (post-Temple) where there is a court

name: Shofar on Shabbat-Rosh HaShanah
notes: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai's institution permitting shofar blowing on Shabbat-Rosh HaShanah wherever there is a court of 23 after Temple destruction

name: Intent When Hearing the Shofar (Kavvanah)
notes: Requirement to intend to fulfill the mitzva when hearing shofar; one who hears from a pit or echo; one who hears from behind a synagogue; comparison to Megillah reading

name: Tekiah, Terua, Shevarim (Shofar Blast Types)
notes: The three types of shofar sounds, their lengths relative to each other, the order of sets (tekia-terua-tekia), and rules about extended tekiot

name: Musaf Blessings of Rosh HaShanah (Malkhuyot, Zikhronot, Shofarot)
notes: The three special blessings of the Rosh HaShanah Musaf Amidah: Malkhuyot (Kingship), Zikhronot (Remembrances), Shofarot (Shofar verses); minimum ten verses each; order of shofar blowing relative to each blessing

name: Zikhronot (Remembrances Blessing)
notes: The Rosh HaShanah Musaf blessing containing verses about God's remembrance of creation, covenant, and deeds

name: Malkhuyot (Kingship Blessing)
notes: The Rosh HaShanah Musaf blessing proclaiming God's kingship with ten biblical verses; debate between R. Akiva and R. Yochanan ben Nuri about its placement

name: Shofarot (Shofar Verses Blessing)
notes: The Rosh HaShanah Musaf blessing containing ten verses mentioning the shofar, from Torah, Writings, and Prophets

name: Prayer Leader Fulfilling Obligation for Congregation
notes: Debate between Rabban Gamliel and sages whether the shaliach tzibbur's prayer fulfills the obligation for individuals who do not know how to pray; context of Rosh HaShanah Musaf

name: Takkanot of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai
notes: Post-Temple institutions by Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai: shofar on Shabbat where there is a court; lulav all seven days outside Temple; prohibition on new grain all day of 16 Nisan; accepting new moon testimony all day

name: Lulav All Seven Days (Zecher laMikdash)
notes: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai's institution that the lulav be taken all seven days of Sukkot outside the Temple, in commemoration of Temple practice

name: New Grain Prohibition Throughout Day of Omer (Zecher laMikdash)
hebrew: איסור חדש כל יום הנף זכר למקדש
notes: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai's institution extending the prohibition on new grain throughout the entire sixteenth of Nisan as a remembrance of the Temple

name: Authority of Beit Din to Sanctify the Month
notes: The principle that the calendar is determined by the earthly court's declaration, not heavenly calculation; Rabban Gamliel's authority even when disputed; submission to court ruling as binding

name: Disqualified Witnesses (Gamblers, Usurers, Dove Racers, Shevi'it Merchants, Slaves)
notes: Categories of people disqualified from giving testimony, as enumerated in Rosh HaShanah: dice players, usurers, pigeon racers, shevi'it merchants, and slaves

name: Trumpets (Chatzotzrot) in Temple Service
notes: Use of silver trumpets alongside the shofar in the Temple on Rosh HaShanah and fast days; rules about when trumpets sound long vs. short blasts

name: Shofar of Yovel vs. Rosh HaShanah
hebrew: שופר של יובל ושל ראש השנה
notes: Comparison between the shofar blown on Yom Kippur of the Jubilee year and that of Rosh HaShanah; debate between R. Yehuda and sages about which horn is used

name: Bnei Maron (Divine Review of All Creatures)
notes: The imagery of all humanity passing before God like sheep (bnei maron) on Rosh HaShanah for divine judgment
